name: Chronic Relapsing Inflammatory Optic Neuritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Chronic Relapsing Optic Neuritis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Two or more episodes of optic neuritis separated by at least 4 weeks
Clinical evidence of optic nerve inflammation including visual loss and pain on eye movement
Exclusion of other causes of optic neuropathy such as multiple sclerosis or neuromyelitis optica
MRI evidence of optic nerve enhancement during acute episodes
Negative aquaporin-4 and MOG antibody testing to exclude other demyelinating diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two episodes of optic neuritis with clinical and MRI evidence of optic nerve inflammation and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent unilateral or bilateral visual loss
searchTerms: repeated vision loss in one or both eyes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Optic disc swelling during acute episodes

common.symptomName: Reduced pupillary light reflex (afferent pupillary defect)
Transient worsening of vision with heat or exercise (Uhthoff phenomenon)
searchTerms: vision worsens with heat or exercise
temporary vision loss after heat exposure

occasional.symptomName: Headache associated with optic neuritis episodes

searchTerms: simultaneous inflammation of both optic nerves

rare.symptomName: Optic atrophy with permanent vision loss
searchTerms: optic nerve damage causing permanent vision loss
degeneration of optic nerve with vision impairment

rare.symptomName: Associated mild systemic constitutional symptoms (fatigue, malaise)

laboratory: Negative myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) antibody test
Normal routine blood tests excluding infectious or systemic inflammatory causes
imaging: MRI showing optic nerve enhancement during acute episodes
Absence of brain lesions typical for multiple sclerosis
genetic: No known specific genetic markers identified
other: Visual evoked potentials showing delayed conduction in affected optic nerve

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of demyelinating brain lesions on MRI
Positive oligoclonal bands in cerebrospinal fluid
More severe and bilateral optic neuritis episodes
Absence of optic nerve inflammation signs

redFlags: Lack of pain with vision loss
Progressive neurological deficits beyond optic neuritis
references: International Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorders, Neurology, 2015
Orphanet: Chronic Relapsing Inflammatory Optic Neuritis, ORPHA:499085
